title: Graphing a Horizontally Compressed and Reflected Two-Thirds Power Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = (-2x)^(2/3) by starting with the standard graph y = x^(2/3) and applying appropriate transformations.
finalAnswer: y = (-2x)^{2/3} = (2x)^{2/3};\quad \text{Parent } y = x^{2/3} \text{ compressed horizontally by } 2;\quad \text{Cusp: } (0, 0),\quad \text{Domain: } (-\infty, \infty),\quad \text{Range: } [0, \infty)

steps.title: Identify the Horizontal Compression and Reflection
steps.explanation: Starting from y = x^(2/3), replacing x with -2x compresses the graph horizontally by a factor of 2 and reflects it across the y-axis. Because y = x^(2/3) is already symmetric about the y-axis, the reflection leaves the compressed graph unchanged.

steps.title: Determine the Cusp, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The graph has a sharp cusp at the origin (0, 0), is defined for all real x, and takes all non-negative values [0, infinity).
steps.why: Horizontal scaling fixes the origin (0, 0) and preserves the range [0, infinity).

steps.title: Find Symmetric Guide Points
steps.explanation: Setting -2x = +/-1 gives x = -/+1/2 with y = 1, and setting -2x = +/-8 gives x = -/+4 with y = 4.
steps.why: Choosing inputs where -2x is a perfect cube (+/-1, +/-8) yields integer y-coordinates.
